extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, journalism students, and newsroom professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A concise set of professional and ethical principles for practicing journalists, stating values and behavioral standards that define good journalism and public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belief in the profession of journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: I believe in the profession of journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms journalism as a distinct, honorable profession and frames subsequent obligations as professional duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism as a public trust / trusteeship
rubrics_metrics.description: The public journal is a public trust; all connected with it are, to the full measure of their responsibility, trustees for the public; acceptance of a lesser service than the public service is betrayal of this trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and others associated with the press must regard their role as serving the public interest above lesser motives or services; betraying that trust is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear thinking, clear statement, accuracy and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear thinking and clear statement, accuracy and fairness are fundamental to good journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic work should emphasize clarity of thought and expression, factual accuracy, and equitable, fair presentation of people and issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity / write what you hold to be true
rubrics_metrics.description: A journalist should write only what he holds in his heart to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should be honest and sincere in their reporting — not publishing claims they do not genuinely believe to be true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against unjustified suppression of news
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppression of the news, for any consideration other than the welfare of society, is indefensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withholding information is only justifiable when necessary for societal welfare; suppression for private or inappropriate motives is unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal integrity and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: No one should write as a journalist what he would not say as a gentleman; bribery by one’s own pocketbook is as much to be avoided as bribery by the pocketbook of another; individual responsibility may not be escaped by pleading another’s instructions or another’s dividends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists must maintain personal honor and integrity, reject bribery (whether direct or indirect), and accept individual accountability rather than hiding behind orders or financial incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single standard across advertising, news, and editorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising, news and editorial columns should alike serve the best interests of readers; a single standard of helpful truth and cleanness should prevail for all; the supreme test of good journalism is the measure of its public service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial considerations must not create different ethical standards; advertising, news, and opinion should all adhere to truthful, helpful, and wholesome standards focused on serving readers and public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should maintain independence from undue influences (political, commercial, or personal) to preserve credibility and serve the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not moved by pride of opinion or greed of power
rubrics_metrics.description: Unmoved by pride of opinion or greed of power
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should avoid letting ego, entrenched opinions, or the pursuit of power affect reporting or editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive orientation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should aim to be constructive — seeking solutions and contributing positively rather than merely sensationalizing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerant but never careless
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should be open-minded and tolerant of differing views while maintaining carefulness in verification and standards; tolerance is not an excuse for laxity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-control
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should exercise restraint and professionalism in judgment, tone, and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should show patience in gathering facts and developing fair, accurate stories rather than rushing to premature conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respectful but unafraid
rubrics_metrics.description: Always respectful of its readers but always unafraid
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain respect for the audience while not shying away from hard truths or challenging powerful interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick indignation at injustice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should be alert to and vocally opposed to injustice, using its voice to expose and challenge unfairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unswayed by privilege or mob clamor
rubrics_metrics.description: Is unswayed by the appeal of privilege or the clamor of the mob
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should resist pressures from elites and popular mobs alike; decisions should be grounded in impartial judgment and public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal chance and human brotherhood
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks to give every man a chance and, as far as law and honest wage and recognition of human brotherhood can make it so, an equal chance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism should promote fairness, equal opportunity, and recognition of shared humanity, supporting social conditions that enable equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patriotism balanced with international goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: Is profoundly patriotic while sincerely promoting international good will and cementing world-comradeship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism may be patriotic but should also foster international understanding and cooperation rather than narrow nationalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism of humanity for today's world
rubrics_metrics.description: Is a journalism of humanity, of and for today’s world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate aim is humane reporting that serves contemporary society and addresses human needs and global connectedness.
